title: Learned soundscape features predict tropical-forest species occurrence
summary: Learned soundscape features predicted occurrence for 34 of 39 surveyed bird and herpetofaunal species across a forest-degradation gradient in Sabah. Predictions used the broader acoustic environment rather than direct identification of every species call. Site-level evaluation supports a bounded monitoring result, not proof of causal habitat quality or a replacement for species surveys.
ai_technology: Convolutional audio embeddings and Gaussian-mixture occurrence models
organization: Norwegian Institute for Nature Research; Imperial College London

evidence.tested: Occurrence predictions were compared with field point counts using cross-validation.
evidence.unknown: Transfer to other ecosystems and causal interpretation are not established by this study.
evidence.ai_role: Convolutional audio embeddings and Gaussian-mixture occurrence models supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher metadata, affiliations, abstract and selected Methods/Results; supplements not reviewed.
